item.title: P0 bug bundle: "Iris during music". — Conversation
item.body:
P0 bug bundle: "Iris during music". The owner reported: "it's vibrating almost all the time", and "when music is playing it's not able to hear me at all — not even when volume is 0". Evidence is in the installed Iris 0.2.15 logs (~/Library/Application Support/Iris/agent.log and ~/Library/Logs/Iris/main.log, 29 Sep 17:10–17:17 IST; main.log timestamps are UTC, 11:40–11:47).

1. "Iris pause mute" (17:13:06) → the DO lane set **system output volume to 0** (`device.set_volume 0`) instead of pausing the music. The music kept playing silently, and Iris's own voice was muted too. Pause, stop and mute must act on the music player; system volume only when the user explicitly says "volume".
2. **The mic stream nearly stopped after the music started:** "stt: streamed 0s of audio in the last minute" at 17:14 and 17:15, and 8 s at 17:16, while the owner was speaking. It was 13–28 s during the music. Suspect the adaptive SendGate floor (the quietest-20-of-100 chunks × 2.5) staying high after loud music, or something else gating the mic. RCA with evidence.
3. **While the music is audible, speech is garbled** ("i disposed", "i just called you a bit", "i respond music"). The music plays via a native player (afplay), outside the renderer's WebRTC AEC, so there's no echo reference. Options: play music through the renderer so AEC cancels it, and/or duck the music on speech onset or the wake word.
4. **A garbled line restarted the music:** "i respond music" → [[PLAY]] a new track. Low-confidence or garbled utterances during music must never trigger play/stop.
5. **"Vibrating":** the dance re-plans every 6–9 s from beat detection with confidence 0.35–0.54, tempo jumping 60–184 BPM. Also the listening micro-motion runs continuously while music keeps the mic busy. Require a confidence threshold (else gentle sway), smooth and clamp the tempo, and don't run the pending micro-motion while merely listening.

**Rules:**
- RCA first with log evidence per item;
- tests that fail before each fix;
- fixes on employee branches;
- QA verifies with real music playing (audible, and at volume 0) on the Mac;
- the lead reviews before merge, then a release as 0.2.16 with owner approval.

**Priority P0:** keep other work paused (the weekly subscription window is at 80%).

item.title: "the music stopped, play it again" pauses the music
item.body: Reproduction (29 Sep, current feat/iris-character): services/agent-svc/app.py _is_stop_music() matches a music noun plus a stop verb by substring, so "stopped" in "the music stopped, play it again" and "the song stopped playing, resume it" is read as a stop command; the negation guard only covers sentences that start with why/what/did/don't. The deterministic MUSIC-STOP intercept (app.py ~3745) then calls experts.call("media","stop") and Iris pauses the music the owner asked to resume. Noted as a separate CR in docs/experts/core.md ("the deterministic _is_stop_music still uses substring verbs"). Expected: a resume/play-again request never stops playback; a real stop ("stop the music", "pause it", "gaana band karo") still does. Work: RCA with the log line, a failing test in tests/test_music_stop.py first, then the fix on your emp/* branch, then report_done with counts; QA verifies. No merge, no release.
